page: Microsoft Azure E16ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores using the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. This instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any GPUs or local storage, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E16ps_v6 demonstrates top-tier memory performance, with its Passmark memory score placing in the top 10% and its large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths ranking in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression also performs in the top 25%. However, compute-heavy and multi-threaded tasks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench workloads, fall into the average category. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in large language model inference, where prompt processing for medium 7B models is weak, placing in the bottom 25%, while text generation for the same model remains average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides a high memory density of 8.0 GB per core, making it a resource-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The instance is well-suited for memory-cached databases, enterprise applications, web serving, and general-purpose workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading.
